name: Seraiah
overview: Seraiah is a male biblical figure identified as the son of Neriah, as recorded in Jeremiah 51:59. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, he is noted possibly to be the brother of Baruch, suggesting a family connection within the prophetic context. His mention is brief but distinct within the scriptural narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Seraiah' is a proper name meaning 'YHWH persists,' 'YHWH is prince,' or 'YHWH contends,' reflecting a theologically rich understanding of God's active presence. This name was not explicitly given by God but carries significant meaning rooted in the divine name YHWH, as noted in Jeremiah 51:59.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Seraiah as the son of Neriah, according to Jeremiah 51:59. There is a suggestion that he may be the brother of Baruch, though this is not definitively stated in the text. Beyond these connections, no additional family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Seraiah's significance lies in his familial link to Neriah and possibly Baruch, individuals associated with the prophetic ministry during Jeremiah's time. His mention in Jeremiah 51:59 situates him within the context of God's dealings with His people, underscoring the continuity of divine purposes through family lines connected to the prophetic mission. Though not extensively detailed, his presence contributes to the broader biblical narrative by highlighting those who served in the prophetic era.
